subject: Dedicated footprint options and GPU runway for CloverTech
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@clovertech.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated footprint options and GPU runway for CloverTech

Dana —

Thanks again for the time today. I put together three dedicated reservation scenarios tailored to the usage profile you shared on the call. Each option includes cluster footprint, minimum guaranteed GPUs, and a suggested 90-day activation/ramp schedule so you can tie capacity to throughput milestones. The attached one-pager and onboarding checklist summarize the operational items.

Quick summary: 
- Minimal Baseline (Cost-optimized): 8 GPUs guaranteed (equivalent to ~2x A100 nodes); reserved burst pool for short spikes; 30-day activation window. Good for predictable steady inference (~100 req/s).
- Growth Ramp (Balanced): Start at 16 GPUs, automated step to 32 GPUs by day 90 (triggers at 30/60/90 days tied to CPU/throughput thresholds); includes staged warm-cache preloads and progressive quantization to reduce unit cost.
- Performance Slate (SLA-first): 48 GPUs baseline with reserved low-latency lanes and hot warm-cache; intended for latency-sensitive production with strict SLOs.

Notes on flexibility: all three models support staged activation, a soft-decommit window (14-day notice), and optional burst credits for unexpected traffic. Pricing will vary by baseline GPU count and reserved throughput lanes — I can send an estimate once you confirm which scenario you want to price.

Next steps: 
1) Confirm preferred scenario or request a hybrid (e.g., Baseline + burst credits).
2) Share procurement contact and PO timing.
3) Book a 30-minute technical alignment with Karthik to finalize activation windows and warm-cache expectations.

Attachments: CloverTech_Dedicated_Options_v1.pdf, runbook_onboarding_checklist.xlsx

Thanks,

Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com

From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@clovertech.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-15T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint options and GPU runway for CloverTech

Mateo —

Appreciate the thoughtful breakdown. A few quick questions before we move to procurement: 
1) For the Minimal Baseline, what is the true minimum we can commit to without impacting latency SLAs? We operate in two regions (us-west, us-east); does the 8-GPU baseline assume a single-region placement?
2) For Growth Ramp, can the ramp triggers be event-based instead of strictly time-based (e.g., X sustained QPS for 7 days)?
3) For Performance Slate, what is the warm-cache preload time and cost implications (do we bill for cache preloading as compute hours)?
4) What are the decommit/change windows once a contract is signed? We may need to scale down after Q1 if feature usage shifts.

Procurement: procurement@clovertech.com is on point for PO timing. They typically need an SOW + line-item pricing. Can you include region-specific pricing? We likely prefer a US multiregional footprint for redundancy.

Thanks — happy to hop on a follow-up call.

Dana Liu
Head of AI Platform | CloverTech

Dana —

Thanks for the detailed questions. Looping in Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (infra) to confirm the technical/ops specifics and region pricing. Quick answers while they jump in: 
- Minimal Baseline: 8 GPUs is single-region by default. For multi-region redundancy we recommend 8 GPUs per region (so 16 total) or a single-region baseline + cross-region failover. Minimums impact latency SLOs in the sense that cross-region tails can increase p99; we'll quantify expected p99 for each placement.
- Ramp triggers: yes — we can make the 30/60/90 activations event-driven (sustained QPS or average token throughput thresholds) instead of calendar-based.
- Warm-cache preload: we bill standard compute hours for preload runs; warm-cache preservation reduces token cost by avoiding cold KV cache misses. I'll let Marissa provide typical preload durations and expected compute cost for your model mix.
- Decommit windows: standard contract allows staged decommit with a 30-day notice and a soft-decommit (partial scale-down) policy with prorated credits; exceptions can be negotiated in the SOW for annual commitments.

Marissa/Karthik — can you confirm the preload duration assumptions for 70B/13B families (approximate KB sizes) and provide region-specific pricing guidance for US-west vs US-east? Dana, we'll aim to include per-region line-items in the next PDF so procurement has everything needed.

Mateo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@clovertech.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-16T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated footprint options and GPU runway for CloverTech

Hi Dana —

Following up with the technical details so you have concrete numbers for procurement: 

1) Minimums & region placement
- Single-region 8-GPU baseline: assumes A100-equivalent nodes with 2 GPUs per node (4 nodes). This setup keeps p50/p90 low for typical inference patterns but p99 can be ~20-40ms higher than a 16-GPU multi-region setup under tail events.
- Multi-region recommendation: 8 GPUs in us-west + 8 GPUs in us-east for active-passive failover (total 16). Active-active is supported but requires cross-region KV syncing and increases baseline cost.

2) Ramp triggers (event-driven)
- We support event-driven triggers: sustained 7-day rolling average of X QPS or sustained token-hours thresholds. Activation is automated and follows a warmup plan: cache preloads -> progressive batching -> quantization rollout.

3) Warm-cache preload and billing
- Preload time: for a 70B family model with a 10GB KV footprint, expect ~2-3 hours of node time for an initial full KV load per region. For 13B family (smaller KV) ~30-45 minutes.
- Billing: preload runs are billed as compute hours at the baseline GPU rate. We typically include a preload credit for first-run on new activations (negotiable for enterprise deals).

4) Decommit/change windows
- Standard: 30-day notice for baseline scale-down and prorated billing for that month. For reserved contracts we offer a 14-day soft-decommit grace for minor adjustments and a 60-day long-tail for larger contractual changes (subject to term negotiation).

I've attached an updated PDF (CloverTech_Dedicated_Options_v2.pdf) with per-region line items, a sample SOW checklist, and an onboarding runbook. If this looks good I suggest we schedule a 30-minute procurement + technical walk-through next week to finalize PO line items and signature authority.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
